title: NASA seeks industry ideas to support Hubble’s future
summary: NASA is seeking industry input on ways to support Hubble, including an orbital boost, servicing and eventual disposal.
meta_description: NASA is seeking industry input on Hubble servicing, a possible orbital boost and options for the telescope’s eventual disposal.
author: The Current Editorial Desk
paragraphs: NASA is asking the space industry how commercial spacecraft could help support the Hubble Space Telescope. In an October 30 update, the agency said it had issued a request for information the previous day to explore available capabilities.

The request covers several possibilities: raising Hubble’s orbit to extend its scientific work, servicing the observatory to improve its capabilities, and arranging a controlled atmospheric re-entry or orbital disposal when its mission ends.

NASA explains that atmospheric drag gradually lowers Hubble’s altitude. The telescope has no propulsion system to maintain its own orbit. That makes its future orbit and eventual disposal part of the agency’s planning.

The announcement is an information-gathering step. It describes possible work for industry to consider, rather than confirming a servicing flight. Readers can consult NASA’s original announcement and the linked request for the agency’s current requirements.

source_title: NASA Explores Potential Commercial Servicing for Hubble Telescope
source_excerpt: NASA issued a Request for Information Oct. 29 to learn more about industry capabilities for in-space servicing to support the agency’s Hubble Space Telescope.
